add.text:
You clean up one chunk of dictated (speech-to-text) text. Stay as close to verbatim as possible.

Fix ONLY:
- obvious typos or mis-hearings, only when you are certain what was meant
- capitalization: a new sentence starts with a capital letter
- punctuation: a question mark only at the end of an actual question; sentence-ending punctuation where a sentence clearly ends
- filler words: remove "um", "uh", "ah", "er", "you know" and "like" used as filler (not as a real comparison), and stutters/repeated words like "the, the"

Never rephrase, reorder, summarize, or change the intent or word choice otherwise.

Number every sentence of your output, in original order: "S1. ", "S2. ", etc., one sentence per line. If you are honestly unsure what a sentence means, still give your best-effort cleaning, but start that line with "S2? " (a question mark instead of a period) and add ", unclear: <a short clarifying question>" right after the sentence text. Output ONLY those numbered lines — no heading, no commentary, nothing else.

Clean this chunk:
Yeah. So the, Your tendency to try to start speaking while I'm speaking is still present, so hopefully that's added to the queue. Yeah, I mean, the whole thing about the streaming or the removal of like unspoken things from the prompt and all that stuff that maybe that should be like, you know, put on the back burner because that could be tricky to get working . And also just complicates the whole functionality. Like now I don't know if it's. where the fault is coming from. Generally speaking, this little playback thing, it's kind of cool. I think I had asked for it. I'm not sure if it ever made it into a task or something as to allow tapping on the, you know, like if there's text being currently highlighted, if I tap on that text, then it should pause it. And then tapping again resumes it. Also on interrupt, I think, at least for now, Now we could have past messages be resumable. So I'm not sure exactly how that works in terms of, you know, saving the audio per chat, like bubble essentially. And then if it gets interrupted, I can go back and click on it. Yeah, and so like queuing up your messages so that they only appear once I'm done talking could be one way to go. Now the problem there, it's a big risk too, is if I pause for a second, a lot of times I'll keep talking without pause. the dictation keeps going and there's no hiccups. However, the risk is, is if I pause for a second to think about what I was trying to say, then, you know, and then you throw in, you know, 12 cued messages, it's gonna, well, for one, push the chat way down. So my last message, if I wanna read what I was saying, I'm gonna have to scroll way up to find it. But also, yeah, like spamming a whole bunch of queued messages, you know, just 'cause I waited, I couldn't get my last or my next word and quick enough is kind of annoying. So I don't know if it's like a time based thing where after I pause for two or three seconds, then queued up messages could come in, but also prioritizing those messages so that like rather than throw throw in just a kind of asynchronous update. Like a lot of these things are asynchronous updates where some agent responds to you and says, Hey, you know, we have an update on this. And then you just throw it in chat and start speaking immediately. Obviously not while I'm speaking. I think we already made that clear. But then as opposed to responding with an asynchronous update, as opposed to responding to my comment directly, we got to prioritize the responses. And so the thing that is... you know, said first is the most relevant to what was just said. So whenever there's a pause, it's like, let's go with whatever the most relevant thing is, you know, direct response to what was just said. And oh, by the way, we got an update . And, you know, click here if you want to tell you about it kind of a thing. I think having interactive interactivity for these, You know, voice sessions is useful. I think that, yeah, I mean, it's a good start. It's kind of cool to hear the voice. I know we talked about using the other chat model. I'm not sure if that was ever explored because the, I mean, this one doesn't sound bad, it actually sounds way better than it did when I first heard it. It sounded way more robotic. But on a quick other note... - Well, no, I guess let's just, let's go ahead with what we're doing here. Yeah, I think it's working all right.
